content.intro: This lesson covers Documentation Tests and Examples. It sits in Module 18, Testing, Debugging, and Documentation, and builds toward a practical Rust mental model rather than memorizing a term in isolation.
content.why_it_matters: Documentation Tests and Examples matters when you work with repeatable quality checks and feedback. Understanding the rule helps you predict compiler or runtime behavior, document assumptions, and choose a safer implementation when inputs or system conditions change.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Reliable code uses tests and diagnostics to make assumptions visible. Unit tests isolate behavior, integration tests exercise public boundaries, and documentation tests keep example code checked alongside the API.

content_blocks.title: A reliable way to reason about it
content_blocks.text: For Documentation Tests and Examples, write down the inputs, the guarantee you expect, and the boundary where that guarantee stops. Work through a minimal example first; then deliberately test one edge case. Make tests deterministic and focused. Documentation examples should be executable where possible, and mocks should not obscure the behavior that matters.

items.text: Try an empty, missing, invalid, unusually large, or concurrently accessed input when that boundary applies to Documentation Tests and Examples. Record what should happen and how you can verify it.

content_blocks.run_instructions: Save as src/main.rs in a Cargo binary. Run cargo run and cargo test; adapt the test shape to the real behavior under review.
content_blocks.reset_steps: Return the sample to its original form, run the documented command again, and compare the result. If a dependency, target, runtime, database, or hardware device is required, configure that separately before treating the result as verified.

content_blocks.title: Common mistake and recovery
content_blocks.text: Do not assume Documentation Tests and Examples guarantees more than it actually does. Reduce a failure to a small reproducer, read the full compiler diagnostic or error value, consult the matching official reference, and change one assumption at a time.

content_blocks.title: Toolchain and execution boundary
content_blocks.text: Course examples are static reference snippets, not executed inside CodeLeaf. Most standard-library examples can be tried in a Rust 2024 Cargo project; specialized networking, database, async, procedural-macro, embedded, and WebAssembly scenarios require the toolchain and dependencies described in their lessons.
